# varm

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/varm)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=varm)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://www.tidyverse.org/lifecycle/#experimental)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/kvasilopoulos/varm/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/kvasilopoulos/varm?branch=master)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/kvasilopoulos/varm/workflows/R-CMD-check/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kvasilopoulos/varm/actions)
<!-- badges: end -->

Fast frequentist and Bayesian vector autoregressions (VAR), structural
identification and local projections (LP) for R, with an Rcpp/RcppArmadillo
engine. Every sampler, bootstrap and identification loop runs in compiled code.

The design idea is **one currency for uncertainty**: the bootstrap, the
asymptotic Monte Carlo and each Bayesian sampler return a `varm_draws` object of
reduced-form draws $(B, \Sigma)$. `irf()`, `fevd()`, `hd()` and `forecast()`, and every
identification scheme (`id_chol()`, `id_longrun()`, `id_sign()`, `id_given()`),
work on that object, so a new estimator inherits all identification schemes and
a new identification scheme works with every estimator.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("kvasilopoulos/varm")
```

A C++ toolchain is required (the package compiles RcppArmadillo code).

## What is in the package

| Area | Methods | Entry points |
|---|---|---|
| Reduced-form VAR | OLS/ML, lag selection (AIC, HQ, SC, FPE), stability, summary | `varm()`, `var_select()`, `stability()` |
| Inference | residual / wild (Rademacher, Mammen) bootstrap, Kilian bias correction, asymptotic Monte Carlo | `draws()`, `irf(ci = )` |
| Dynamics | IRF, FEVD, historical decomposition, forecasts; unit-impact normalisation and cumulation | `irf()`, `fevd()`, `hd()`, `forecast()` |
| Identification | Cholesky, Blanchard-Quah long-run, sign restrictions (Haar rotations), user-supplied impact matrix | `id_chol()`, `id_longrun()`, `id_sign()`, `id_given()` |
| Bayesian VAR (conjugate) | Normal-inverse-Wishart with Minnesota, sum-of-coefficients and single-unit-root priors; closed-form marginal likelihood; hierarchical hyperparameters (GLP) | `bvarm()`, `prior_minnesota()` |
| Bayesian VAR (triangular) | Minnesota, SSVS and horseshoe priors; stochastic volatility (KSC mixture) | `bvarm(prior = prior_triangular())`, `volatility()` |
| Local projections | LP, LP-IV, lag augmentation, Newey-West / HC standard errors, cumulative responses | `lp()` |
| Proxy-SVAR | external-instrument identification with wild bootstrap | `varm_proxy()`, `proxy_fstat()` |

## Example

The `yraw` data set holds three quarterly US series (inflation, unemployment,
interest rate; Koop and Korobilis, 1953Q1-2006Q3).

```{r example}
library(varm)
y <- as.matrix(yraw); colnames(y) <- c("inflation", "unemployment", "rate")

fit <- varm(y, p = 2)
fit
```

Responses to a policy-rate shock (recursive identification, rate ordered last) with
wild-bootstrap bands:

```{r irf, fig.height = 3.2}
ir <- irf(fit, id = id_chol(), horizon = 16, ci = "wild", nboot = 300)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 0.6), mgp = c(1.7, 0.5, 0))
for (v in colnames(y)) {
  b <- ir$bands[v, "rate", , ]; h <- 0:16
  plot(h, ir$estimate[v, "rate", ], type = "n", ylim = range(b), xlab = "horizon", ylab = "", main = paste("rate ->", v))
  polygon(c(h, rev(h)), c(b[, 1], rev(b[, 4])), border = NA, col = adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.2))
  polygon(c(h, rev(h)), c(b[, 2], rev(b[, 3])), border = NA, col = adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.3))
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey60"); lines(h, ir$estimate[v, "rate", ], lwd = 2, col = "steelblue4")
}
```

The same call works for a Bayesian VAR (hierarchical Minnesota prior; exact draws
for the coefficients given the hyperparameters, Metropolis for the
hyperparameters):

```{r bvar}
bfit <- bvarm(y, p = 2, ndraw = 1000, nburn = 500)
bfit
irb <- irf(bfit, id = id_chol(), horizon = 16)
round(irb$estimate["unemployment", "rate", c(1, 5, 9, 17)], 3)
```

and a local projection of the same response:

```{r lp}
lp(y, shock = "rate", horizon = 16, lags = 2, contemp = c("inflation", "unemployment"), lag_augment = TRUE)
```

## Learn more

* `vignette("var-theory")` - reduced-form VAR: definitions, IRF/FEVD/HD, bootstrap and Monte Carlo inference.
* `vignette("identification")` - Cholesky, long-run and sign restrictions; Fry-Pagan; normalisation.
* `vignette("bayesian-var")` - NIW posterior, Minnesota/unit-root priors, GLP hyperparameters, SSVS, horseshoe, stochastic volatility, diagnostics, comparison with `BVAR`.
* `vignette("local-projections")` - LP, LP-IV, lag augmentation, LP versus VAR bias-variance.
* `vignette("choosing-a-method")` - decision guide and a map of the VAR/LP literature and R packages (after [awesome-var](https://github.com/kvasilopoulos/awesome-var)).
* `docs-src/methods-index.md` - index of every method with its reference and where it is implemented.

## Related packages

`vars`, `svars`, `BVAR`, `bsvars`, `bsvarSIGNs`, `lpirfs`, `BigVAR`, `bvartools`:
see `vignette("choosing-a-method")` for how `varm` relates to them. Results for
the reduced-form VAR agree with `vars` to machine precision, and the hierarchical
BVAR agrees with `BVAR` (same prior inputs) up to Monte Carlo error.

## Status

The package is experimental. See `NEWS.md` for the change log.
